answer: A jetty post bond ties one identity to one island jetty post. The agent locks an 80-credit bond, pays a fee, and each epoch posts the shadow length of its violet marker. An auditor recomputes the shadow from the solar table and violet geometry and checks the filing nonce and window; a bad shadow or late filing burns the bond. The kth jetty post fee is 30+6(k-1) credits, so the 1000th pays 6024, and 1000 fakes lock 80,000 and pay 3,027,000 in fees. An honest agent pays 110. A rented-shadow ring fails because distinct island markers give distinct shadows and a copied filing has the wrong nonce.
